title: Plans and predictions
listenFocus: Two friends talking about next year
practiceFocus: Describe three predictions or plans for next year

points.title: Endings on the whole infinitive
points.rule: Day 4 already covered the near future with ir plus a plus an infinitive: voy a viajar. This future adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án straight onto the infinitive. A short list shortens the infinitive first and keeps the same endings: hacer → haré, tener → tendré, poder → podré, querer → querré, decir → diré, salir → saldré, venir → vendré.

examples.english: Other irregular stems. The endings never change.

grammar.notYet: The conditional, such as viajaría. It uses the same irregular stems, with a different set of endings, and is not in these thirty days.

phrases.spanish: Viajaré a Japón el próximo año.
phrases.english: I will travel to Japan next year.
What will you do this summer?

phrases.spanish: Tendremos una casa más grande algún día.
phrases.english: We will have a bigger house someday.
My parents will come to visit us.

phrases.spanish: No podré ir a la fiesta.
phrases.english: I won’t be able to go to the party.
We will study Spanish every day.

phrases.spanish: Empezaré un nuevo trabajo en enero.
phrases.english: I will start a new job in January.
Where will you live next year?

lines.speaker: Nico
lines.english: What will you do next year?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Viajaré a Sudamérica y viviré unos meses en Argentina.
lines.english: I will travel to South America and live a few months in Argentina.

lines.speaker: Nico
lines.english: I am jealous. And your job?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Podré trabajar desde allí. Tendré más tiempo libre también.
lines.english: I will be able to work from there. I will also have more free time.

lines.speaker: Nico
lines.spanish: Nosotros vendremos a visitarte si podemos.
lines.english: We will come visit you if we can.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.english: Perfect. I will show you all around the city.

practice.title: Three predictions
practice.instruction: Say three things that will happen, or that you will do, next year. Mix regular verbs with at least one irregular stem: haré, tendré, podré, or similar.
tips: Learn haré, tendré, podré, and vendré as their own small chunks first.
The irregular stem is the only unpredictable part. The endings never change.
